reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: § 24.1 grants Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor (notice only), § 24.2 requires our prior written consent (reasonableness qualified) for any Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance or change-of-control transfer, and bars assignment to a direct competitor, and § 24.4 expressly negates any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration or service-reduction right on our change of control.
§ 24.3's residual consent requirement is scoped to 'other assignments', so it does not undercut the § 24.1 carve-out; § 13.3 aligns licence transfer with permitted Section 24 assignments.

No redline or counterparty comment is expected for a compliant finding, and the deterministic check confirms the successor/affiliate carve-out is present; nothing in the cited paragraphs approaches the walk-away triggers.
Only minor nuance (Vendor's competitor bar is consent-overridable rather than absolute) does not warrant reclassification as a deviation given the overall preferred-position match.
